messages:
Alex Kim: RFC follow-up — I sketched a pragmatic approach for the seams between Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Goal: single abstract deployment interface + small adapters that translate control-plane intent to env specifics. Thoughts?

Maya Singh: love the direction. worried about auth and network differences. private deploys have KMS/HSM + mTLS to internal services. adapters need hooks for key rotation and egress rules. :thinking: 

Raúl Ortega: agree. add mandatory capability flags on adapters: {auth, kms, egress, secrets, observability}. adapters must surface unsupported capabilities at startup, not at runtime.

Samir Patel: startup-time capability negotiation is good. Also need a fallback policy in control plane: if a feature isn't available on Private, route to Dedicated/Hosted when allowed by policy.

Natalie Cho: +1. But for privacy-regulated tenants, fallback may be illegal. Need per-tenant policy enforcement and a strict deny option.

Alex Kim: yep — policy enforcement belongs to the control plane. Proposed data model: AdapterCapabilities proto with boolean flags and version string. Control plane keeps compatibility matrix and rollout rules.

Maya Singh: can we avoid protobuf proliferation? maybe JSON schema for adapters and a lightweight capability endpoint: `GET /_adapter/capabilities` returning
```
{"capabilities": {"kms": true, "egress": false}, "adapter_version": "0.9.2"}
```
This keeps adapters simple to implement.

Raúl Ortega: fine. but for latency-critical routing we need typed, small payloads — favor compact JSON over verbose proto on the agent->control-plane path.

Samir Patel: need to define clear translation rules for model pinning and rollout semantics. Hosted can fallback to a quantized variant; Private may have local model with different weights. How do we express equivalence?

Natalie Cho: propose an 'equivalence class' id on models. Control plane maps requested model -> adapter-candidate models with equivalence IDs and a confidence score. Adapters can reject if confidence < threshold.

Alex Kim: good. Also propose a simulator mode for adapters so we can run integration tests against a 'dry-run' adapter that reports capabilities and simulates latency/throughput.

Maya Singh: +1 for simulator. It should allow injecting failure modes: high latency, kv-cache misses, partial kv population — helps test graceful degradation and fallback.

Raúl Ortega: about observability: adapters must emit a unified trace header and token-level metric tags. Control plane will aggregate but adapter must expose per-request metadata: `x-rd-trace` header and `X-Adapter-Cap` set.

Samir Patel: security note: adapters must not log full prompts. Provide redaction helper lib (shared) and a strict default config that redacts by type.

Natalie Cho: rollout plan: 1) capability endpoint + simulator, 2) implement adapters for Dedicated (small) and Private (k8s/hw), 3) publish control-plane mapping UI and policy flags, 4) run canary tenants.

Alex Kim: timeline suggestion: 4 weeks for spec + simulator, 6 weeks for two adapters POC, then 2 weeks integration. Adjust if infra bandwidth low.

Maya Singh: will add a doc with the capability schema and simulator API tomorrow.

infra-bot: deploy-checker: RFC doc updated at https://redwood.internal/rfcs/190 - CI lint OK :rocket: 

Alex Kim: thanks all. Action items: Maya write schema, Raúl prototype simulator, Samir draft model-equivalence spec, Natalie define policy knobs. I'll update the RFC with these decisions.

Maya Singh: done. I'll ping this thread when the schema PR is up. :thumbsup:
